newsitem.title: USA: NBA-SUNS GUARD JOHNSON QUESTIONABLE WITH SPRAINED ANKLE.
newsitem.headline: NBA-SUNS GUARD JOHNSON QUESTIONABLE WITH SPRAINED ANKLE.

text.p: Phoenix Suns point guard Kevin Johnson is listed as questionable for Thursday night's playoff game against the Seattle SuperSonics due to a sprained left ankle.
Johnson suffered the injury when Seattle forward Shawn Kemp knocked him over from behind while chasing a loose ball in the fourth quarter of the Suns' 110-103 victory on Tuesday.
The Suns hold a 2-1 lead in the best-of-five Western Conference series.

Johnson, who said he plans to retire after the season, is the leader of the Suns' four-guard offence. Seattle has keyed its defence on Johnson with various traps, which has allowed numerous open shots for guards Rex Chapman, Wesley Person and Jason Kidd.

Chapman hit a playoff-record nine three-pointers and scored a career-high 42 points in the Suns' series opening win at Seattle last Friday. Person had 29 points and Chapman scored 23 points to lead Phoenix to Tuesday's win.
Johnson had 22 points in Tuesday's victory, but hit just 6-of-17 field goal attempts and is shooting 26 percent in the series.
Johnson missed 12 games due to hamstring problems this season. He averaged 20.1 points and 9.3 assists in 70 games.
